title: Program terminates with pending promises
body:
Take a file fetch.js with content:
```js
fetch("https://www.google.com/").then(x=>console.log(x));
```
Executing with `bun run fetch.js` terminates without any logging while doing `deno run fetch.js` prints the actual content of the response.

Other problem, adding await in front of everything, like:
```js
await fetch("https://www.google.com/").then(x=>console.log(x));
```
prints
```
[0.05ms] "node_modules.bun" - 1 modules, 1 packages
[native code]
```
instead of the relevant response.

promise.then(() => console.log(1));/
new Promise((resolve) => resolve(promise)).then(() => console.log(3));/
new Promise((resolve) => promise.then(resolve)).then(() => console.log(2));"

1
3
2

1
2
3

1
3

Browsers and node shows `1, 2, 3`.

From my personal perspective it isn't obvious and weird, but I assumes an engine should follow the spec.

title: Allow explicitly hoisting certain packages using `public-hoist-pattern`

labels.name: bun install
labels.description: Something that relates to the npm-compatible client

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun, like pnpm, doesn't automatically hoist packages to the root `node_modules` folder. This is the right thing to do. However, there are a handful of scenarios where we genuinely do need to hoist transitive dependencies. One of those scenarios is when we use the [`better-typescript-lib`](https://github.com/uhyo/better-typescript-lib) package.

This package, as the name describes, provides better type definitions for the built-in typescript libraries. For example, it provides stricter type definitions for `JSON.parse`, `JSON.stringify`, and `fetch().json()`, which helps developers catch more bugs at compile time. All you need to do to use this library is install it. It provides the type definitions as transitive dependencies.

```
  /better-typescript-lib@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6):
    resolution:
      {
        integrity: sha512-LMFX7HPN5qlJiW5IlJiicTT2XcJJ8wRTq3D1YinmZzqNQ0lKX409EK+4cmkuMZTkfyZXBxOca29zvZwIGt9Q3Q==,
      }
    peerDependencies:
      typescript: ">=4.5.2"
    dependencies:
      "@typescript/lib-decorators": /@better-typescript-lib/decorators@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-dom": /@better-typescript-lib/dom@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2015": /@better-typescript-lib/es2015@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2016": /@better-typescript-lib/es2016@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2017": /@better-typescript-lib/es2017@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2018": /@better-typescript-lib/es2018@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2019": /@better-typescript-lib/es2019@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2020": /@better-typescript-lib/es2020@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2021": /@better-typescript-lib/es2021@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2022": /@better-typescript-lib/es2022@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es2023": /@better-typescript-lib/es2023@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es5": /@better-typescript-lib/es5@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-es6": /@better-typescript-lib/es6@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-esnext": /@better-typescript-lib/esnext@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-scripthost": /@better-typescript-lib/scripthost@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      "@typescript/lib-webworker": /@better-typescript-lib/webworker@2.4.0(typescript@5.1.6)
      typescript: 5.1.6
    dev: true
```

These transitive dependencies, such as `@typescript/lib-es5`, are hoisted to the root `node_modules` folder by package managers like yarn and npm. And, when the TypeScript compiler sees `@typescript/lib-*` packages in the root `node_modules` folder it replaces the built-in type definitions for that library with the type definitions provided by the package. For example, the type definitions in `es5.d.ts` would be replaced by the type definitions provided by `@typescript/lib-es5`.

Unfortunately, because bun doesn't hoist packages, we can't use `better-typescript-lib` with bun. This is a shame, because `better-typescript-lib` is an indispensable package for me. I ❤️ both bun and `better-typescript-lib`. It would be awesome if I could use both of them together.

### References

- [`better-typescript-lib`: How it works](https://github.com/uhyo/better-typescript-lib#how-it-works)
- [TypeScript 4.5 Release Notes: Supporting `lib` from `node_modules`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-4-5.html#supporting-lib-from-node_modules)


### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Like bun, pnpm also doesn't automatically hoist packages to the root `node_modules` folder. However, it does provide an escape hatch, [`public-hoist-pattern`](https://pnpm.io/npmrc#public-hoist-pattern), which can be used to hoist only certain packages. Thus, we can use `better-typescript-lib` with pnpm by adding the following line to our `.npmrc` file.

```
public-hoist-pattern[]=@typescript/*
```

I especially like this solution, because we're being explicit about which packages we want to hoist. And, as the [Zen of Python](https://peps.python.org/pep-0020/) states, "Explicit is better than implicit." It would be awesome if bun also implemented the `public-hoist-pattern` config option. Implementing something like `public-hoist-pattern` in the `bunfig.toml` file would be the easiest way to enable `better-typescript-lib` to be used with bun.

### References

- [`better-typescript-lib`: Installation with pnpm](https://github.com/uhyo/better-typescript-lib#with-pnpm)

### What alternatives have you considered?

There are three alternatives here.

1. 😢 Don't use bun. I would have to fall back to using pnpm again, which is not bad, but I would love to use bun.
2. 😭 Don't use `better-typescript-lib`. If I want to continue using bun then I'd have to give up on using `better-typescript-lib`, which is currently a deal-breaker for me.
3. 🤔 Change `better-typescript-lib` to somehow work with bun. As one of the contributors of the `better-typescript-lib` package, I could try to find a solution to make `better-typescript-lib` work with bun. However, I have absolutely no idea how to make it work with bun. If there's a way to make `better-typescript-lib` work with bun by making a change in `better-typescript-lib` itself, then I'm all ears.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

When I throw an error in an async function, the stack trace correctly includes the full call stack, showing the sequence of function calls leading to the error. However, if an `await` statement (e.g., `await Promise.resolve(true)`) is added before throwing the error in the same async function, the resulting stack trace becomes incomplete. Specifically, it omits critical details about the call hierarchy, reducing the stack trace to only the line where the error is thrown, without referencing the calling function(s).

**Steps to Reproduce:**

```ts
async function throwError() {
  throw new Error();
}

async function run() {
  await throwError();
}

run();
```

      at /redacted/path/to/index.ts:10:1
```

  await Promise.resolve(true); // Added this line

title: Feature Request: Zero-Installs Support (Vendored Dependency Cache for Offline Installs)

labels.name: bun install
labels.description: Something that relates to the npm-compatible client

body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

This feature would solve the problem of build and deployment failures caused by npm or other package registry outages. Currently, `bun install` requires access to the remote registry to fetch dependencies unless they are already cached globally. This creates reliability issues for scheduled scripts, CI/CD pipelines, and offline or air-gapped environments, where network access to registries can be intermittent or unavailable. By enabling zero-installs through a vendor dependency cache checked into the repo, Bun could ensure fully offline installs, improve build reproducibility, reduce external dependencies, and increase overall resilience and developer productivity.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

I’m proposing a zero-installs feature similar to Yarn’s Zero-Installs model, where dependencies are vendored and cached within the project (e.g., a `.bun/cache` folder) and committed to source control. This would allow `bun install` or `bun run` to operate entirely offline by using the vendored cache and lockfile, eliminating the need to access remote registries during installs or script runs. Additionally, a config option or flag (like `--cache-only`) could enforce offline-only behavior for deterministic and reliable builds.

### What alternatives have you considered?

I’ve considered relying solely on Bun’s global cache, but it doesn’t guarantee consistency or reproducibility across different machines or CI environments. Another alternative is manually archiving and restoring the `.bun/install/cache` directory in CI, but this approach is error-prone, not standardized, and adds operational overhead. Switching to Yarn Zero-Installs is a workaround but doesn’t align with using Bun as the primary tool.

 macOS (Darwin 24.6.0, arm64)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

  1. Create a new directory and run `bun init`
  2. Install Hono v4.9.4: `bun add hono@4.9.4`
  3. Create server.js with minimal Hono app:

  ```javascript
  import { serve } from 'bun';
  import { Hono } from 'hono';

  const app = new Hono();

  app.get('/health', (c) => {
    return c.json({ status: 'ok', timestamp: new Date().toISOString() });
  });

  const port = parseInt(process.env.PORT || '3000');
  const server = serve({
    port,
    fetch: app.fetch,
  });

  console.log(`Server running on http://localhost:${port}`);
  export default server;

  4. Run: bun server.js
  5. Test any endpoint: curl http://localhost:3000/health

### What is the expected behavior?

HTTP requests should return JSON responses:
  - GET /health should return: {"status":"ok","timestamp":"2025-08-28T01:18:20.083Z"}
  - Server should handle requests normally (sans current error)


### What do you see instead?

All HTTP requests fail with "Maximum call stack size exceeded" error.

  Instead of JSON, requests return an HTML error page with:
  - Title: "GET - /health failed"
  - Error: "ExceptionOccurred" → "RangeError" → "Maximum call stack size exceeded"
  - No stack trace or useful debugging information

  The server starts successfully but every single HTTP request triggers this stack overflow.

### Additional information

Root Cause: This appears to be a runtime compatibility issue between Bun's serve() function and Hono v4.9.4's internal
  architecture.

  Evidence:
  - Same code works perfectly with Node.js + @hono/node-server
  - Issue persists with absolutely minimal Hono apps (no middleware, no external dependencies)
  - Tested with latest Bun v1.2.21 - issue still occurs
  - Works fine with Hono v3.x

  Workarounds:
  - Downgrade to Hono v3.x: bun add hono@3
  - Use Node.js runtime instead of Bun
  - Switch to Bun-native frameworks like Elysia

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.10+30e609e08

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create `test.js` with a literal null byte (0x00) between the backticks:
```js
const s = String.raw``;
console.log("length:", s.length);
console.log("charCode[0]:", s.charCodeAt(0));
```

Run with `bun test.js` and `node test.js`.

### What is the expected behavior?

```
length: 1
charCode[0]: 0
```

A null byte in a template literal should be preserved as-is, matching Node v22.22.0 behavior.

### What do you see instead?

```
length: 6
charCode[0]: 92
```

Bun outputs the 6-character literal string `\uFFFD` (`\`, `u`, `F`, `F`, `F`, `D`) instead of a single null byte.

### Additional information

Bun version: `1.3.10+30e609e08`  
Node version: `v22.22.0` (reference)

Ran into this with [`wasm-audio-decoders`](https://github.com/eshaz/wasm-audio-decoders), which uses [`simple-yenc`](https://github.com/eshaz/simple-yenc) to embed WASM binaries as yEncoded strings in template literals, decoded at runtime via `String.raw`. Every decoder (`mpg123-decoder`, `flac`, `ogg-vorbis`) failed with a CRC mismatch because null bytes in the payload were being corrupted by the transpiler.

Workaround was applied in simple-yenc (escape null bytes on encode, treat `0xFFFD` as `0x00` on decode) but the root cause is in Bun.

title: iterating a `Set<number>` corrupts large epoch-millisecond values
Map/Set lose distinct integer keys ≥ 2^31 on 1.4.0-canary (regression)
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0-canary.1+b3d086e26

### What platform is your computer?

WSL

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

# `Map` and `Set` merge distinct integer keys ≥ 2³¹  (canary 1.4.0 regression)

## What version of Bun is running?

`1.4.0-canary.1` -- revision `b3d086e26f3a6fc39733316d7af7b1d661fe81c6` (`oven/bun:canary`).

Every stable release tested is **unaffected**: `1.3.5`, `1.3.13`, `1.3.14`, `latest`.
This is a regression on the `1.4` line.

## What platform is your computer?

`Linux x64 (baseline)` -- WSL2, kernel `6.6.87`, glibc `2.41`.
Also reproduced cleanly in the official `oven/bun:canary` Docker image, so it is not
environment-specific.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const a = 1779314400000; // a millisecond timestamp
const b = 1779400800000; // a different timestamp, one day later

console.log(a === b); // false -- these are two distinct numbers

const m = new Map();
m.set(a, "A");
m.set(b, "B");

console.log(m.size);   // 1   ← expected 2
console.log(m.get(a)); // "B" ← expected "A"
console.log(m.get(b)); // "B"

console.log(new Set([a, b]).size); // 1 ← expected 2
```

`Map` and `Set` treat **every integer-valued number key with magnitude ≥ 2³¹** as the
same key. It is not just a hash-bucket collision -- the keys compare *equal*, so
membership is wrong too:

```js
const m = new Map([[2 ** 40, "only-key"]]);
console.log(m.has(2 ** 41)); // true ← expected false (never inserted)
```

## What is the expected behavior?

`m.size === 2`, `m.get(a) === "A"`, `new Set([a, b]).size === 2`,
`m.has(<never-inserted-key>) === false` -- i.e. distinct numbers are distinct keys.
This is what Node.js, every browser, and every stable Bun release do.

## What do you see instead?

The second `set()` overwrites the first. `get()` / `has()` on any large-integer key
resolve to the most-recently-inserted large-integer entry. All large-integer keys
behave as a single equivalence class.

## Additional information

### Boundary -- the defect starts exactly at 2³¹ (the signed 32-bit limit)

| Key | canary 1.4.0 |
|-----|--------------|
| integers in `[-(2³¹-1), 2³¹-1]` | ✅ correct |
| integers `≥ 2³¹` | ❌ all merge into one key |
| integers `≤ -2³¹` | ❌ all merge into one key (incl. `INT32_MIN`) |
| non-integer doubles (e.g. `2³² + 0.5`) | ✅ correct |
| plain object property keys | ✅ correct |

```js
new Map([[2 ** 30, 1], [2 ** 30 + 1, 2]]).size  // 2  ok
new Map([[2 ** 31, 1], [2 ** 31 + 1, 2]]).size  // 1  BUG
new Map([[2 ** 32, 1], [2 ** 33, 2], [2 ** 34, 3]]).size  // 1  BUG (all three merge)
```

- A small (in-range) integer never collides with a large one -- `0` vs `2³²` stay
  distinct. Large integers only collide *with each other*.
- Non-integer doubles take a different, correct path; only **integer-valued** numbers
  are hit.

### Regression matrix

| Bun | revision | result |
|-----|----------|--------|
| `1.3.5`  | `1e86cebd74a5723e818b5c0555276b646bcf0e4c` | ✅ correct |
| `1.3.13` | `bf2e2cecf27e800962b1e7f03d66278f9d5d2e79` | ✅ correct |
| `1.3.14` | `0d9b296af33f2b851fcbf4df3e9ec89751734ba4` | ✅ correct |
| `1.4.0-canary.1` | `b3d086e26f3a6fc39733316d7af7b1d661fe81c6` | ❌ **bug** |

### Likely cause

The boundary is exactly 2³¹ and non-integer doubles are unaffected, which suggests the
new (`1.4`) `Map`/`Set` implementation has an integer key fast-path that only handles
`i32`, and the fallback for integers outside that range produces both a constant hash
**and** a broken key-equality comparison.

### Real-world impact

This is not a contrived case. It surfaced as a production bug where a dashboard
aggregated values into a `Map<number, Bucket>` keyed by a period `Date.getTime()`.
Every `Date.now()` value (~`1.7e12`) is in the broken range, so all buckets collapsed
into one and every period reported the grand total. Keying a `Map`/`Set` by a timestamp
is an extremely common pattern.

### Reproduction

Two `docker run` commands -- no local Bun needed, only the image tag differs:

```sh
# stable -- prints "Map size: 2" (correct)
docker run --rm oven/bun:latest bun -e 'const m = new Map([[2**32, "a"], [2**33, "b"]]); console.log("size", m.size, "get(2**32)", m.get(2**32))'

# canary -- prints "Map size: 1" (bug)
docker run --rm oven/bun:canary bun -e 'const m = new Map([[2**32, "a"], [2**33, "b"]]); console.log("size", m.size, "get(2**32)", m.get(2**32))'
```

---

*Possibly separate issue:* on the same canary build, running a script located at the
filesystem root (`bun /script.mjs`) panics with
`panic: cannot resolve DirInfo for non-absolute path`. Stable Bun runs it fine. This is
unrelated to the `Map` bug and may warrant its own report.

### What is the expected behavior?

### What do you see instead?

title: Error.captureStackTrace(err, fn) removes too many frames — zod v4 .parse() errors end up with an empty stack
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14+0d9b296af

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 24.4.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// repro.mjs
class MyError extends Error {}

function makeError() {
  const err = new MyError('boom')
  Error.captureStackTrace(err, makeError)
  return err
}

function caller() {
  return makeError()
}

console.log(caller().stack)
```

Run with `bun repro.mjs` and `node repro.mjs`.

### What is the expected behavior?

V8 drops the frames above and including the function passed as the second argument, the callers below it stay. Node 22.21.1:

```
Error: boom
    at caller (file:///private/tmp/repro.mjs:10:10)
    at file:///private/tmp/repro.mjs:13:13
    at ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:343:25)
    at async onImport.tracePromise.__proto__ (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:665:26)
    at async asyncRunEntryPointWithESMLoader (node:internal/modules/run_main:117:5)
```

### What do you see instead?

`caller` is gone too:

```
Error: boom
    at /private/tmp/repro.mjs:13:13
```

So bun cuts at least one frame more than node. Depending on the shape of the callee it cuts everything, see below.

### Additional information

How we hit this: zod v4 calls `Error.captureStackTrace(err, inst.parse)` on every failed `.parse()` (`zod/v4/core/parse.js`, the callee is the arrow assigned in `zod/v4/classic/schemas.js`). Under bun the resulting ZodError has zero frames:

```js
import { z } from 'zod'

const schema = z.object({ schema: z.object({}) })

function initPlugin() {
  return schema.parse({})
}

try {
  initPlugin()
} catch (e) {
  console.log(e.stack)
}
```

With zod 4.3.6, bun prints just the message and not a single `at` line. node keeps the call site:

```
    at initPlugin (file:///private/tmp/zr.mjs:6:17)
    at file:///private/tmp/zr.mjs:10:3
    at ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:343:25)
```

In practice any zod validation error in a bun app is undebuggable from logs. We found this when a dependency threw a ZodError during server startup and the log couldn't say where from.

Things I checked:

- `// @bun` at the top of the file changes nothing, so this doesn't look like the transform issue from #24789 / #16704
- `safeParse()` (zod passes no callee there) keeps the frames fine
- #6923 was about the same API, but it's closed and this is current 1.3.14
